children: Emkay Global Financial' research report on Mahindra Finance

Supported by broad-based disbursement growth, benign asset quality, and contained credit cost, MMFS reported a healthy 2QFY27. PAT was up 55% yoy to Rs8.82bn and AUM rose ~15% yoy to Rs1.47trn, aided by strong momentum in the non-wheels segment. GS2+GS3 fell to a multiyear low of 8.1%, with the usual seasonal deterioration in 2Q largely absent. Management sees existing overlays of Rs8.52bn as an adequate cushion against external stress, and currently sees no need to build more. However, it flagged near-term headwinds: rising COF amid rate hikes, draft insurance-commission norms that could dent fee income, drought-related collection risk, and softer early festive demand, particularly in tractors. Margins remain at the lower end of the level needed for target ROA, though the drag from excess liquidity and trade advances should ease. Management retained its medium-term guidance on growth, credit cost, and ROA, and said the MRHFL merger is on track. Factoring in these near-term headwinds, we cut our FY27-29 estimates, resulting in a 1-2% cut in our FY27- 29E EPS.
We maintain BUY while lowering our Sep-27E TP by ~10% to Rs370 (Rs410 earlier), implying FY28E PBV of 1.7x.
